item.title: How to Become a Mangler in COD Warzone (Haunted Hollow Research Center Easter Egg)
item.description:
Haunted Hollow is here for Call of Duty: Warzone 's Season 6: The Haunting update, and it's filled with Easter Eggs. While players may be grinding to unlock the Crimson Crawler Camo, they can also get a bunch of items from Zombies, like the Ray Gun. However, you may have also seen a Mangler walking about, and this is actually tied to the EMF Reader Easter Egg at the Research Center. Here is how to become a Mangler in Warzone .

All COD Black Ops 7 Season 6 BlackCell Camo Challenges

Call of Duty: Black Ops 7 Season 6 releases with new BlackCell Camos to earn. Here is how to unlock every Season 6 BlackCell Camo Challenges.

By Nathan Round

Step #1: Find the EMF Reader

Before you can even begin the Easter Egg, you will need to find the EMF Reader , which you may likely have already come across. The EMF Reader can be found in the server room of the building to the south-east of the Research Center , particularly on the bottom floor. Once you find it, grab it to secure it in your Tactical Slot and then head to the Research Center.

Step #2: Grab the Weapon with a Thermal Optic

For the next step, you will need to find a weapon with a Thermal Optic. While you can create a loadout with one, there is actually a Voyak KT-3 in the Research Center with one already equipped. You can find this gun on the top floor towards the center of the south portion of the building , just by a whiteboard. Grab it, because you will need it for the next step.

Step #3: Use the EMF Reader & Thermal Optic to Hunt Three Ghosts

Now that you have both items, you will need to use them to hunt down three spirits in the Research Center. To do this, first pull out your EMF Reader to find the location of the ghost. The EMF Reader will display a Low, Medium, or High reading depending on how close you are to the ghost. The aim is to get the reading to reach 9.99 , which will indicate that you are in the room with the spirit.

Once you are near the ghost with the reading on High, the room will go black. From here, use your Thermal Optic to locate the ghost. It should take the form of a random object with a particle effect. Once you find it, shoot it to move the spirit to a new location. You will need to repeat this step a total of three times. However, you do have a limited time to do so. If you fail to find the ghost, you will receive a jump scare, and it will move to another location.

Successfully finding and shooting the spirit three times will drop a bunch of rewards, including a Mutant Injection. Using this item will turn you into a Mangler from Zombies for a short period of time, where you can use the Mangler Cannon, melee players with your sickle, or simply down them with your sprint attack.

item.title: Final Fantasy & 4 Other RPGs Officially Unplayable Nowadays
item.description:
On September 30, Final Fantasy 14 Mobile shuts down its servers in China , killing any plans for a global expansion. Roughly a week later, Square Enix ends Final Fantasy 7 Ever Crisis ' life, bringing to a close a project with a lot of untapped potential. These impending stoppages got me thinking about all the RPGs that have gone the way of the Dodo, doomed forever to an existence confined to people's memories, "do you remember" pieces, and dead icons.

Final Fantasy alone is responsible for hundreds of hours of delisted content, even if spin-off games like Brave Exvius and Mobius were never held in high esteem by the community. There is a sadness in the knowledge that you will never be able to boot up a specific game again, and it's a shame so much good work has been largely erased from history. So let's try to keep the memories of a few of these dead RPGs alive; if nothing else, they should serve as a lesson for the future.

All these games shut down long ago, so this article is a retrospective tribute (in some cases, anyway). That said, if you plan to play Ever Crisis again, do it now.

Also, the word is "officially," so some of these RPGs might be playable through unofficial means. I'll include a note if you can still play them in some form.

Dissidia Final Fantasy: Opera Omnia Was A Fantastic RPG

Square Enix Finally Got A Mobile Game Right, And It Is Now Dead

  • Launch Date: February 1, 2017
  • End Date: February 29, 2024
  • Was It Any Good? Yes. A genuinely great game.
  • Any Way To Play It Nowadays? Unfortunately, no. There isn't a public fan server or custom APK that really lets you play beyond booting up the home menu. Square Enix preserved most of the cutscenes, at least.

As will repeatedly happen over the next few weeks, Square Enix regularly shuts down Final Fantasy games, to the point that any new mobile release feels destined for a premature end. While I believe each of these projects should be preserved, most were pretty bad and mostly served as examples of what to avoid when adapting a popular franchise for Android and iOS.

Surprisingly, the best mobile Final Fantasy RPG came from the subseries that is famously not part of that genre: Dissidia Final Fantasy: Opera Omnia . Developed by Square Enix and Team Ninja, Opera Omnia beautifully adapted the mainline entry's real-time arena combat into a turn-based system that can 100% stand alongside the classic Final Fantasy games. The "Bravery" system required the use of non-damage strikes to inflict the "Break" status and manipulate the turn order, all leading to HP attacks.

Square Enix Game is Permanently Shutting Down on October 6

Square Enix announces the shutdown date and time for one of the games in its beloved and ongoing Final Fantasy franchise.

By Joshua Duckworth

Unlike modern gacha games, Opera Omnia was incredibly player-friendly, with every character unlocking through story progression and events. Weapons used a gacha system, but they were pretty easy to get since premium currency wasn't in short supply. The roster featured more than 150 characters across the franchise, bringing together mainstays like Cloud and Squall with lesser-known figures like Kadaj and Type-O 's students. Even the writing was pretty good, and the characters' interactions didn't feel like just cheap fanservice.

Frankly, Opera Omnia 's death was a genuine tragedy, and the gaming world lost something special on February 29, 2024. Square Enix's refusal to release an offline mode was infuriating; honestly, the publisher could repackage the game as a solo RPG, and it would probably perform well.

Infinity Blade Trilogy Is Dead But Thriving

The Best iOS RPGs Of All Time, Kept Alive By Fans

  • Launch Date: December 9, 2010 (First game)
  • End Date: December 10, 2018 (All three games)
  • Was It Any Good? All the games are top-notch action RPGs.
  • Any Way To Play It Nowadays? Yes, you can play all three games, though not through official means. Infinity Blade 1 and 2 were reverse-engineered into native PC ports. The third entry doesn't have a PC port, but dedicated players have managed to boot the mobile game using Sideloadly and older iOS versions. It isn't a flawless option, but the game is at least still playable. You can still play the first two RPGs through a similar method, too.

Unlike Dissidia Final Fantasy: Opera Omnia , which is completely dead in every conceivable way, the Infinity Blade trilogy is only officially unplayable. Opera Omnia ended because it relied on Square Enix's servers; these games, meanwhile, suffered from outdated software and Apple's closed ecosystem. All three RPGs were neglected to the point that they couldn't run on new iOS versions, but they're still playable with the right software and a player's willingness to think outside the box.

The Infinity Blade trilogy succeeded because its mechanics are designed around a touchscreen. Rather than turning a screen into a compromised controller, they use an iPhone's unique features to craft an experience tailor-made for the platform. Chair Entertainment treated your finger as a blade's edge; for instance, parrying required reading an enemy's movement and swiping against their action's trajectory. The combat was great and a true selling point for the series.

Shin Megami Tensei: Imagine Is The Ultimate Nightmare Scenario

Killed And Then Killed Again

  • Launch Date: April 4, 2007
  • End Date: May 24, 2016 (In Japan); January 29, 2014 (In Western Nations)
  • Was It Any Good? Flawed but decent. The Western version was worse than the Japanese one, though.
  • Any Way To Play It Nowadays? Fan servers exist, so you can still play the game. However, Atlus and Sega sued these attempts in the early 2020s, nuking into oblivion any easy-to-find public versions. Methods still exist, but they are far more complicated to follow.

Considering Atlus' franchise went truly mainstream with Persona 5 , there is a good chance that plenty of players completely missed out on Shin Megami Tensei: Imagine , an ambitious MMO that was already dead in Western nations by early 2014. While most franchises disconnected MMOs from their mainline entries, Imagine sought to bridge the gap between the first two SMT games, which feature widely different worlds.

Embracing SMT 's dark fantasy and sci-fi themes, the developers dropped players into a post-apocalyptic hellscape that has subterranean shelters and on-the-ground ruins. The setting feels oppressive, which makes complete sense for the franchise as a whole. SMT 's turn-based combat got a real-time makeover that surprisingly kept much of the original's appeal, including the demon negotiation mechanic.

Atlus abandoned Imagine without an offline version, so community members built playable fan servers, including two of the most famous: ReIMAGINE and COMP-Hack. Atlus and Sega didn't like that and filed a lawsuit, which essentially killed these accessible ways to play the game and made future endeavors feel illegal.

Fortnite Spin-Off & 4 Huge Games Officially Shutting Down

Over the next few months, Epic Games shuts down a Fortnite mode, and Rocket Racing is one of a couple of major games shutting down.

By Mark Sammut

Darkspore Proves That Single-Player Games Can Die Too

Time For The EA Entry

  • Launch Date: April 26, 2011
  • End Date: March 1, 2016
  • Was It Any Good? Yes, pretty darn good.
  • Any Way To Play It Nowadays? Fans have made parts of Darkspore accessible, but the combat isn't one of them.

All these closures are frustrating in their own right, but Darkspore is the most egregious, as its demise was totally avoidable and completely unnecessary. While mainly known for its 4-player co-op, this action RPG featured a full single-player campaign that basically aped Diablo , albeit with a few neat ideas implemented from Spore .

Although not one of the all-time greats, Darkspore was a solid isometric action RPG that stood out for its three-creature squad system and loot that included body parts as equipment/gear. The gameplay was quite fun, as you could swap between your creatures with the click of a button.

EA implemented always-on DRM, meaning the game had to be constantly online; when the servers shut down, the single-player portion became unplayable, and the physical disc became a paperweight. The funny thing is that Darkspore would probably not be remembered at all if it wasn't murdered for no good reason; otherwise, it would just be another Diablo -clone that filled the void until Diablo 3 's release.

Babylon's Fall Was Always Unplayable

Born A Corpse

  • Launch Date: March 3, 2022
  • End Date: February 27, 2023
  • Was It Any Good? No.
  • Any Way To Play It Nowadays? No.

OK, let's end things with the ultimate cautionary tale: Babylon's Fall . Square Enix hired one of the greatest developers of single-player action romps, PlatinumGames, to craft a live-service treadmill. Despite seeming like a bad idea from its reveal, this RPG somehow ended up being far worse than anybody could have imagined, to the point of being basically unenjoyable throughout its entire life. In less than a year, Square Enix shut down this disaster, confirming years of wasted resources and time.

I'm not going to pretend that Babylon's Fall deserved better, as it was an ugly game developed through cynical trend-chasing. However, PlatinumGames was kind of onto something with the Gideon Coffin concept, which let you equip two physical and two spectral weapons at the same time. You attacked with all of them simultaneously, which could have made for a fun combat system for a standard 15-hour adventure.

7 Turn-Based RPGs With Perfect Progression Systems
5 Near-Perfect Party-Based RPGs With No Weak Links

item.title: World of Warcraft Is Stealing Two of Final Fantasy 14's Best Features
item.description:
World of Warcraft will add controller support and remove some transmogrification restrictions, both of which have already been done by its main competitor Final Fantasy 14 . However, both upcoming World of Warcraft features have some noticeable caveats for players to consider.

It's no secret that World of Warcraft and Final Fantasy 14 are two of the biggest titles in the MMORPG genre. Though each title offers different takes on hotkey-based combat, that has not stopped Blizzard and Square Enix from drawing inspiration from one another. One key example is World of Warcraft 's player housing system, which used FF14 's own housing as an example of how each game differs in implementing similar ideas. While Final Fantasy 14 player housing has limited plots per server, WoW 's housing system generates new neighborhoods as needed.

World of Warcraft Reveals Big Changes For One of Midnight's Most Popular Classes

Blizzard reveals that more players will soon be able to play as one of Midnight's most popular classes in the expansion's climactic content update.

By James Ratcliff

World of Warcraft Gains Controller Support, Drops Some Transmog Restrictions

Soon, Blizzard's long-standing game will add two more features inspired by its rival. Following the reveal of World of Warcraft: Forever during BlizzCon's opening ceremony, attendees discovered that official controller support would be available in the upcoming title. By comparison, Final Fantasy 14 has supported controllers from the game's beginning, which now includes support for PlayStation, Xbox, and Switch 2 gamepads out of the box. During a BlizzCon 2026 panel to discuss the future of Midnight , the World of Warcraft development team also revealed that armor restrictions on transmogrification sets will be removed in Patch 12.2.5. This means that classes that are known for wearing a specific armor type, such as Paladins in plate armor, can change their gear to look like cloth or leather armor.

However, both controller support and the transmogrification update each come with catches that players should bear in mind. First, Patch 12.2.5's planned transmogrification changes will not apply to specific weapons and to class-exclusive armor sets. As an example, players will not see a Hunter wielding a two-handed mace while wearing the Paladin's iconic Judgment armor set. Additionally, official controller support in World of Warcraft is currently exclusive to Forever . It is unclear if support will extend to Midnight or any of WoW 's Classic game modes. Currently, Midnight players must rely on add-ons to play the game with a controller. Gamepad support is currently available within the WoW: Forever closed beta test. Players can access the World of Warcraft: Forever beta by either opting into it and being chosen at random via email or by purchasing the Skyborne Epic Pack or Warcraft Forever Collection on the Battle.net Shop.

The removal of armor restrictions on transmogrified gear in World of Warcraft will arrive nearly a year after Final Fantasy 14 made a similar move. FF14 's Patch 7.4, Into The Mist, launched on December 16. One of Patch 7.4's key features was the removal of glamour restrictions on armor and accessories, including restrictions based on jobs and levels. Although weapon restrictions still remain to keep animations consistent, FF14 producer and director Naoki Yoshida said that the change was made to fulfill a long-standing player request.

During a BlizzCon 2026 panel to discuss the future of Midnight , the World of Warcraft development team also revealed that armor restrictions on transmogrification sets will be removed in Patch 12.2.5. This means that classes that are known for wearing a specific armor type, such as Paladins in plate armor, can change their gear to look like cloth or leather armor.

However, both controller support and the transmogrification update each come with catches that players should bear in mind. First, Patch 12.2.5's planned transmogrification changes will not apply to specific weapons and to class-exclusive armor sets. As an example, players will not see a Hunter wielding a two-handed mace while wearing the Paladin's iconic Judgment armor set. Additionally, official controller support in World of Warcraft is currently exclusive to Forever . It is unclear if support will extend to Midnight or any of WoW 's Classic game modes. Currently, Midnight players must rely on add-ons to play the game with a controller. Gamepad support is currently available within the WoW: Forever closed beta test. Players can access the World of Warcraft: Forever beta by either opting into it and being chosen at random via email or by purchasing the Skyborne Epic Pack or Warcraft Forever Collection on the Battle.net Shop.

item.title: Last of Us Director Comments on God of War Laufey
item.description:
Former Naughty Dog game director Bruce Straley apologized to the God of War Laufey development team after comments he made during an interview made the rounds on social media. Straley's mention of God of War Laufey was part of a broader discussion about the gaming industry in 2026.

During his time at Naughty Dog, Straley started as an artist for Crash Team Racing and the Jak and Daxter trilogy before working his way up as a co-art director for Uncharted: Drake's Fortune . Straley went on to direct Uncharted 2: Among Thieves , The Last of Us , and Uncharted 4: A Thief's End , each of which is considered among the best stories in PlayStation's library of console-exclusive games. Straley left Naughty Dog in 2017 after an 18-year career and went on to create Wildflower Interactive, an independent game studio, in March 2021.

Insomniac Responds to Marvel's Wolverine AI Accusations

A director for Insomniac Games officially responds to claims that the recently released Marvel's Wolverine uses AI art assets.

By Michael Brandon Ingram

Bruce Straley Apologizes After Mentioning God of War Laufey During Industry Discussion

Following an interview with Edge Magazine that discussed the state of the gaming industry, Straley used God of War Laufey as an example of how he felt AAA games were "boring" and lacking in innovative ideas despite also utilizing impressive graphics. Since then, the former Naughty Dog staffer took to Twitter to clarify his answer. Straley posted his apology to the God of War Laufey development team on September 18 and said that his example was used out of context. He later said that he believed major studios were lacking in risks and innovation within the AAA space and stated that it is not the fault of the developers. Straley said that he felt video games were unique due to being interactive experiences and stressed that studios should continue to push the boundaries of creativity to avoid losing the audience.

To add to his point, Straley claimed that the overwhelming success of games-as-a-service games like Fortnite , Roblox , and Overwatch has "eroded" the ability for studios to innovate and take risks. The former Uncharted director said that trying to replicate the success of the aforementioned titles was not a viable strategy for the gaming industry and claimed that there was a lack of "good leadership" from the people in charge. Straley wrapped up his apology by stating, "I stuck my foot in my mouth and mentioned Laufey, and that was my mistake."

Wishlist Today

Straley and his team at Wildflower Interactive are currently working on a new puzzle-platform title called Coven of the Chicken Foo t, which was first unveiled during The Game Awards 2025. The plot of the upcoming fantasy title focuses on a witch named Gertie, who is joined by a mysterious companion on her journey through dark catacombs and plundered caves. The game's narrative will be unveiled through the environment and the discoveries that players will make. Though Coven of the Chicken Foot has no release date as of this writing, interested players can wishlist it on Steam.

item.title: Fallout 76 Is Giving a Classic Fallout Curiosity More Life Than It Ever Had
item.description:
The new Fallout 76 update is here, and it's putting the spotlight on a random piece of series lore that hasn't really been heard of since Fallout 3 . Each Fallout game features its own special quirks that expand the franchise in interesting ways, and Fallout 3 's Pint-Sized Slasher is one of the strangest and most intriguing parts of the entire game. Now, Fallout 76 is bringing the Pre-War serial killer back into the spotlight with its newest story update, aptly named The Slasher.

The Slasher launches alongside Fallout 76 Season 26, Beware the Blood Moon, and it's abundantly clear that the Bethesda team behind the multiplayer Fallout spin-off is gearing up for Halloween. As spooky season waits around the corner, plenty of live-service games jump at the chance to bring holiday-themed cosmetics and events to players ahead of time, and Beware the Blood Moon and The Slasher are doing just that. What makes The Slasher particularly interesting, though, is that it demonstrates that Fallout 76 could be the prime stage to revive points of lore from past games that deserve another moment in the spotlight.

New Official $7,299 Fallout Release Confirmed

Bethesda's Fallout gets a physical release with pricing that starts at $7,299.

1
By Joshua Duckworth

Fallout 76's Season 26 Update Brings Back Fallout 3's Pint-Sized Slasher in an Unexpected Way

The easiest way for Bethesda to bring Fallout 76 would simply be through another cosmetic bundle, but that thankfully isn't the case. Instead of just a run-of-the-mill killer clown skin, the Pint-Sized Slasher is making his way to Fallout 76 by being the main star of The Slasher quest line. A series of murders have been wreaking havoc on the Appalachian wasteland, and the pattern looks an awful lot like the same methods that the legendary Pint-Sized Slasher used. There are a lot of unsolved mysteries in Fallout , but players will get the chance to dive into these strange killings and solve a mystery of their own.

A Refresher on the Pint-Sized Slasher's Fascinating Lore

Before the bombs fell in Fallout 's Great War, there were rumors of a child serial killer, hence the name Pint-Sized Slasher. The Pint-Sized Slasher was said to have worn a clown mask and was reportedly responsible for the Linden Street slayings that struck fear into Pre-War Washington D.C. Whether the Pint-Sized Slasher was an actual killer or not is murky, because his reputation turned him into a bit of an urban legend that Americans across the country reveled in.

The Pint-Sized Slasher was even used as a myth to scare children into behaving well. Parents would tell kids that if they acted out of line that the Pint-Sized Slasher would crawl out of a dog house and chase them with a knife. Well, that's an absolutely terrifying image to think about, but that isn't even the half of it. The Pint-Sized Slasher eventually became a fascination of Vault 112 scientist Dr. Stanislaus Braun. There are tons of disturbing Vault experiments in Fallout , and Vault 112 is one of the most spine-chilling.

When it comes to the games, Fallout 76 has been keeping the franchise afloat for nearly eight years now. The good news is that new Fallout games are on the way. Fallout 3 and New Vegas remasters are in the works, plus Obsidian and Bethesda are each working on new entries, with the latter taking on main entry Fallout 5 .

As the overseer of Vault 112, Dr. Braun created a virtual simulation machine that the Vault Dwellers were placed in. Each Vault Dweller was fully aware that they were in a simulation, with the assumption being that they would be given a perfect life as the apocalypse loomed outside the Vault. Unfortunately, Dr. Braun was an absolute madman and eventually created a simulation where the Pint-Sized Slasher terrorized a happy suburban town.

Fallout 76 Demonstrates That Fallout's Best Side Lore Doesn't Have to Be Resigned to a Single Game

Of course, not every single piece of Fallout side lore is going to be a good fit for a Fallout 76 update. Old lore like the Pint-Sized Slasher is a perfect fit, though, and the way that Fallout 76 is approaching it brings an extra level of fun to this franchise cameo. An interactive murder mystery is a great way to drum up some Halloween hype while also staying in line with the Fallout franchise's staple vibe.

How Fallout 76's The Slasher Event Works

  • The event is scheduled to last for several weeks.
  • Emergency radio broadcasts bring breaking news to players, updating them on leads and murder details.
  • Infestations are cultists who have become obsessed with the Pint-Sized Slasher.

The main mystery at the center of The Slasher is whether the killer truly is the Pint-Sized Slasher or not. Since the urban legend has made way for obsessive fans to form cults around the killer, it could simply be a copycat. Fallout 76 has always embraced the tradition of cults in Fallout , but the cultists have focused on worshiping cryptids like the Mothman and the Interloper for the most part. Whether someone's worshiping a giant moth-like cryptid or a serial killer tied up in an urban legend, the Fallout games know how to have fun when it comes to building whacky new cults.

Fallout 76 may have taken a while to finally become a satisfying spin-off, but the years of improvements have made way for fun seasonal events like The Slasher and Beware the Blood Moon. Of course, Fallout 76 still isn't the perfect live-service experience that a lot of fans have craved, but the game still serves as a solid way to pass the time while waiting for a new Fallout game.

Obsidian's New Fallout Game Is Actually a Bigger Deal Than Fallout 5
Fallout Season 3's Best Possible Release Window Feels Almost Too Obvious
Fallout 3 and New Vegas Remasters' Best Launch Strategy Is Clear
New Official Fallout PS5 Release Confirmed for September 15

Now that the Pint-Sized Slasher is back in the spotlight, it's going to be interesting to see what other strange pieces of past Fallout lore will come back in a new way. Beyond Fallout 76 , it will be even more exciting to see what secrets and mysteries are in store for the new Obsidian Fallout game and Fallout 5 's stories. Only time will tell, so while fans wait to see what the future of Fallout holds, Fallout 76 has found a strong way to pay homage to the franchise's more bizarre lore bits.
